subsystems.name: Contact skin and transducer array
subsystems.role: deforms against objects and converts force into a measurable signal.

subsystems.name: Readout electronics
subsystems.role: scans many sensing elements quickly and converts analogue signals to digital.

subsystems.name: Mechanical mounting
subsystems.role: attaches the sensor to a robot finger or gripper without distorting measurements.

subsystems.name: Signal processing unit
subsystems.role: turns raw force maps into texture, slip and contact-geometry estimates.

subsystems.name: Calibration and interface
subsystems.role: ensures readings are comparable over time and sends them to the robot controller.

buildSteps.title: Design the array
buildSteps.detail: Choose spatial resolution, force range and skin stiffness for the target objects.

buildSteps.title: Mould the elastomer skin
buildSteps.detail: Cast silicone or a similar elastomer in a mould, sometimes with embedded markers or conductive particles.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Deposit or print conductive traces and sensing electrodes on a flexible substrate using photolithography or screen printing.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the layers
buildSteps.detail: Bond the skin to the electrode layer and encapsulate it so it survives repeated contact.

buildSteps.title: Connect the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Attach the flexible circuit to readout boards with multiplexers and analogue-to-digital converters.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Press the sensor with known weights and indenters to map raw signals to force and shear.

buildSteps.title: Train and test
buildSteps.detail: Collect data while sliding across textures, train a classifier, and validate on a robot gripper.

buildSteps.title: Integrate
buildSteps.detail: Mount on a gripper, connect to the robot controller, and test precision handling tasks.

prerequisites.why: to make dense electrode arrays that bend with the skin.
the skin must deform repeatably and resist wear.
tiny capacitance or resistance changes must be measured accurately.
texture classification and slip detection work in labs but need more robust training data.
precision handling requires both sensing and dexterous, force-controlled motion.

pathway.milestone: tactile arrays and optical sensors in research and niche industrial grippers
pathway.unlocks: reliable detection of contact, force and simple textures.

pathway.milestone: sensor fusion with vision and proprioception
pathway.unlocks: robots that can identify and handle unfamiliar objects.
safe human-robot collaboration and whole-arm manipulation.
general-purpose robots for manufacturing, surgery and service work.
